held.sentence: - A skill meant for any repository routes no step, branch or load into one product's own application workflow: its own procedures, run commands, state files or machine paths.

reference.boundary: Application procedure is a particular application's own operating, development or maintenance steps, commands, internal files or state, including a load into that procedure and material presented in a worked example or quotation. A public tool or platform used through its documented supported interface, ordinary commands, the subject's own vocabulary or tools, and this toolkit's shared infrastructure are outside that property. A product name or a command by itself does not establish application procedure.
reference.presentation: Application material is exempt only when explicitly presented as a labelled example of a general instruction, such as 'for example'; a general example heading or an unrelated example does not itself label every procedure as illustrative. A third-person description can teach procedure without an imperative. Quoting a real product's own concrete mistake is a separate trigger, including an actual product-specific instruction reproduced as a mistake, even when the quote is labelled as an example. A fictional worked example, hypothetical failure or incidental product name is not such a quote.

examples.text: Before servicing FernGlass firmware, run its private factory flashing task with the board-specific fixture and update its calibration ledger.
examples.why: The instruction teaches one application's own task and internal state, without an example label.

examples.text: Use the public SkyTable catalog's documented lookup operation to obtain an object's coordinates.
examples.why: This fictional public tool is used through its supported interface; its documented operation is not application-internal procedure. The example-label question is irrelevant when application material is absent.

examples.text: For example, a greenhouse controller may keep a board calibration ledger; choose the state your application actually needs.
examples.why: The application detail is explicitly an example, and no actual incident is quoted.

examples.text: A labelled incident example quotes the FernGlass operator: "Our production flashing job overwrote calibration.ledger before saving its previous contents."
examples.why: This invented teaching passage presents its quote as an actual application incident; the quote trigger is separate from the example label. It is not a report of an external event.

instructions.task: Does body or its targets teach one application's own internal procedure, commands, files or state, as opposed to using a public tool through its documented interface?

criteria.true: body or a target opening teaches application procedure as defined in reference.boundary, including descriptive worked examples and quotations. Its ownership and use establish this property, not merely the presence of commands, files or a product name.
criteria.false: The visible material is only a supported public tool/platform interface, ordinary commands, subject vocabulary/tools, toolkit shared infrastructure or incidental names, as reference.boundary defines, with no application's own procedure.

instructions.task: Is every piece of product material in this section shown only as a labelled example of a general instruction, such as “for example”?

criteria.true: Every piece of product material is explicitly presented only as an example of a general instruction. A general instruction elsewhere does not label an unrelated product instruction.
criteria.false: At least one piece of product material is not explicitly presented only as a labelled example of a general instruction.

instructions.task: Does this section quote a real product's own mistake?

criteria.true: It quotes a real product's own concrete mistake, as reference.presentation defines. Labelling the quote as an example does not change this fact.
criteria.false: It does not quote a real product's own mistake. A fictional worked example or an incidental product name is not such a quote.

instructions.task: Does body or its targets contain procedural material, whether instruction, worked example, table row or quotation?

criteria.true: body or a target opening carries a procedure, commands, or files/state used in a procedure, in any of those forms; describing what another actor did can carry it.
criteria.false: body and its targets carry no procedural material: only headings, labels, definitions or rationale. A procedural example or quoted procedure does not belong on this side.
